## Waypoint

Waypoint is a self-hosted travel app for one household: a Python backend (`waypoint/`) and a Svelte web app (`frontend/`) that show the trips each member is on (flights, hotels, rental cars, trains, cruises, with their confirmation numbers and costs), keep the household's loyalty and Known Traveler numbers, and read booking emails from members' Gmail mailboxes privately, on the server. Members sign in through OIDC; an AI assistant can be connected over `/mcp` with scopes the household grants. `AGENTS.md`'s "Waypoint's promises" are the app's reasons to exist, and a change that breaks one is a blocking bug whatever else it does: "Email stays on the server", "You see the trips you're on", "IDs are for the household" and "Times are where they happen". Read them, "Mistakes that keep coming back" and "Conventions" (the paved paths lint enforces) first; `SECURITY.md` says what the auth, encryption and mailbox code protects.

## Private data here

The repository is public. Private data is anything read from a real person's instance or mailbox: a traveller's or household member's name, an email address, a confirmation code or record locator, a loyalty, frequent-flyer or Known Traveler number, a flight number with its date, a hotel or stay with its dates, an itinerary, a street address, a Gmail message id, a mailbox's label ids, a passkey or VAPID key, a token, a sign-in URL with a code in it, or the subject, sender, snippet or text of a real email. It would land in a test, a fixture under `tests/fixtures/` (the `.eml` files there are made-up emails with invented names, codes and numbers; real airport codes, airline and hotel names are fine), the demo data (`waypoint/domain/demo.py`, every traveller, booking and code in it made up), a screenshot in `docs/src/assets/screenshots/` (which must show only the demo data), a docs page, a code comment, a commit message or a pull request description, often while explaining a bug. A real-looking name, code, number or address in any of these is a blocking finding; describe a real case in general terms.

## Generated files and the checks that cover them

Left out of the diff you read but listed: `docs/openapi.json` and `frontend/src/lib/api-types.ts` (the API contract, from the routes and `waypoint/server/contract.py`; `make api-contract-check` in `make check` and CI fail when stale), `docs/feature-map.json` and `docs/src/content/docs/contributing/feature-map.md` (the feature map, from the routes, the web app, the tests and the docs; `make feature-map-check` fails when stale and when a route has no test). Also generated, and read in full: `.claude/skills/verify-waypoint/references/cli.md` (from `tools/control`'s help) and `references/feature-map.md` (from the verify pages and flows), both held current by the fleet checks. Lockfiles (`poetry.lock`, `frontend/package-lock.json`, `docs/package-lock.json`) are left out and installed by CI.

## Where things are

`waypoint/server/api/` holds the HTTP handlers, `routes.py` the route table, `domain/` what the app works out from its data (`visibility.py` is the one place trips and segments are queried for a person; `mail/` the parsers, the scan, the cleaner `safe_html.py` and the AI fallback), `providers/` the outside services (`gmail.py`, `mailimages.py`, `webpush.py`), `storage/` the database, `secretbox.py` (encryption at rest), `stored_mail.py`, `gate_codes.py`, `backup.py` and the Alembic migrations. `tls.py` is the only module that opens outbound connections, `oidc.py` sign-in. `tests/` are `unittest` suites; `tests/privacy.py`'s `no_leaks` and `tests/test_every_route.py` are the checks the promises name. `frontend/src/lib/email-render.ts` renders a kept email a second time from its own allowlist, `offline.ts` and `offline-vault.ts` the encrypted copy on a device, `api.ts` the one place that calls `fetch`. `.semgrep/waypoint.yml` holds the paved-path and promise rules with their examples under `.semgrep/examples/`.
